value.body: Some CMAs add a Chartered Accountancy (CA) or Company Secretary (CS) qualification. CA adds statutory audit, attestation and deeper financial reporting; CS adds company law, corporate governance and secretarial compliance. Both institutes give CMA students an entry point that skips their first level.

items.label: Into CA
items.note: For those who have passed the CMA Intermediate; CA Foundation is skipped

items.label: Into CS
items.value: Direct entry to CS Executive; CSEET exempt
items.note: For those who have passed the CMA Final; exemption fees apply

items.label: CA practical training
items.note: Required under the ICAI scheme even with direct entry

items.label: CA Intermediate, both groups (May 2025)
items.note: All CA Intermediate candidates, not only CMA direct-entry students

items.label: CA Intermediate, single group (May 2025)
items.value: Group I ~15% pass; Group II ~22% pass
items.note: ~97,000 sat Group I and ~72,000 sat Group II

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Register with ICAI for CA Intermediate under the direct-entry route, or with ICSI for CS Executive after passing CMA Final. Check each institute's current rules on paper exemptions and fees before registering.

value.title: At a glance
items: CA needs several more years, including articleship; CS is usually shorter.
CMA + CS fits compliance, secretarial and governance roles; CMA + CA fits audit and financial reporting.
A second qualification adds value mainly when the target role needs it — e.g. statutory audit signing (CA) or company secretary posts (CS).

value.title: CA Intermediate, May 2025: appeared and passed
value.note: All CA Intermediate candidates, not only CMA holders. Pass rates about 14.7% (Group I), 21.5% (Group II) and 13.2% (both groups). Pass rates vary by session.
value.source: ICAI CA Intermediate May 2025 result, as reported
